From daa24603d9f0808929514ee62ced30052ca7221c Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Caleb Sander Mateos <csander@purestorage.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Dec 2025 17:19:49 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] ublk: clean up user copy references on ublk server exit

If a ublk server process releases a ublk char device file, any requests
dispatched to the ublk server but not yet completed will retain a ref
value of UBLK_REFCOUNT_INIT. Before commit e63d2228ef83 ("ublk: simplify
aborting ublk request"), __ublk_fail_req() would decrement the reference
count before completing the failed request. However, that commit
optimized __ublk_fail_req() to call __ublk_complete_rq() directly
without decrementing the request reference count.
The leaked reference count incorrectly allows user copy and zero copy
operations on the completed ublk request. It also triggers the
WARN_ON_ONCE(refcount_read(&io->ref)) warnings in ublk_queue_reinit()
and ublk_deinit_queue().
Commit c5c5eb24ed61 ("ublk: avoid ublk_io_release() called after ublk
char dev is closed") already fixed the issue for ublk devices using
UBLK_F_SUPPORT_ZERO_COPY or UBLK_F_AUTO_BUF_REG. However, the reference
count leak also affects UBLK_F_USER_COPY, the other reference-counted
data copy mode. Fix the condition in ublk_check_and_reset_active_ref()
to include all reference-counted data copy modes. This ensures that any
ublk requests still owned by the ublk server when it exits have their
reference counts reset to 0.

Signed-off-by: Caleb Sander Mateos <csander@purestorage.com>
Fixes: e63d2228ef83 ("ublk: simplify aborting ublk request")
Reviewed-by: Ming Lei <ming.lei@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Jens Axboe <axboe@kernel.dk>

diff --git a/drivers/block/ublk_drv.c b/drivers/block/ublk_drv.c
index cfd2132410dd..49c208457198 100644
--- a/drivers/block/ublk_drv.c
+++ b/drivers/block/ublk_drv.c
@@ -1607,8 +1607,7 @@ static bool ublk_check_and_reset_active_ref(struct ublk_device *ub)
 {
 	int i, j;
 
-	if (!(ub->dev_info.flags & (UBLK_F_SUPPORT_ZERO_COPY |
-					UBLK_F_AUTO_BUF_REG)))
+	if (!ublk_dev_need_req_ref(ub))
 		return false;
 
 	for (i = 0; i < ub->dev_info.nr_hw_queues; i++) {
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of the Patch

This patch fixes a reference count leak in the ublk driver that occurs when a ublk server process exits while there are still outstanding requests dispatched to it. The leak was introduced by a previous commit that optimized request failure handling but inadvertently omitted the reference count decrement for certain data copy modes.

### Modifications in `drivers/block/ublk_drv.c`

- **Line 1610 (changed condition):**  
  The original conditional check explicitly tested for two flags (`UBLK_F_SUPPORT_ZERO_COPY` and `UBLK_F_AUTO_BUF_REG`).  
  It is replaced with a call to the helper function `ublk_dev_need_req_ref(ub)`, which returns `true` for **all** reference-counted data copy modes (including `UBLK_F_USER_COPY`).

### Relationships between the Modifications

The change is a single, targeted replacement of a hard-coded flag check with a more comprehensive helper function. The relationship is straightforward:
- The previous condition only covered zero-copy and auto-buffer-registration modes, leaving `UBLK_F_USER_COPY` unprotected.
- The updated condition now correctly includes all modes that require reference counting, ensuring that any requests still owned by the exiting server have their reference counts reset to zero.
- This prevents both the reference count leak and the associated warning triggers (`WARN_ON_ONCE` in `ublk_queue_reinit()` and `ublk_deinit_queue()`).

Here is the commit message:
ublk: clean up user copy references on ublk server exit

If a ublk server process releases a ublk char device file, any requests
dispatched to the ublk server but not yet completed will retain a ref
value of UBLK_REFCOUNT_INIT. Before commit e63d2228ef83 ("ublk: simplify
aborting ublk request"), __ublk_fail_req() would decrement the reference
count before completing the failed request. However, that commit
optimized __ublk_fail_req() to call __ublk_complete_rq() directly
without decrementing the request reference count.
The leaked reference count incorrectly allows user copy and zero copy
operations on the completed ublk request. It also triggers the
WARN_ON_ONCE(refcount_read(&io->ref)) warnings in ublk_queue_reinit()
and ublk_deinit_queue().
Commit c5c5eb24ed61 ("ublk: avoid ublk_io_release() called after ublk
char dev is closed") already fixed the issue for ublk devices using
UBLK_F_SUPPORT_ZERO_COPY or UBLK_F_AUTO_BUF_REG. However, the reference
count leak also affects UBLK_F_USER_COPY, the other reference-counted
data copy mode. Fix the condition in ublk_check_and_reset_active_ref()
to include all reference-counted data copy modes. This ensures that any
ublk requests still owned by the ublk server when it exits have their
reference counts reset to 0.

Signed-off-by: Caleb Sander Mateos <csander@purestorage.com>
Fixes: e63d2228ef83 ("ublk: simplify aborting ublk request")
Reviewed-by: Ming Lei <ming.lei@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Jens Axboe <axboe@kernel.dk>

Here is the root cause:
The bug is a reference count leak in the ublk driver when a server process exits with outstanding requests. The function `ublk_check_and_reset_active_ref()` only reset references for requests using `UBLK_F_SUPPORT_ZERO_COPY` or `UBLK_F_AUTO_BUF_REG`, but not for `UBLK_F_USER_COPY` (another reference-counted data copy mode). This omission occurred after commit e63d2228ef83 optimized request failure handling by skipping the reference count decrement in `__ublk_fail_req()`. Consequently, requests in `UBLK_F_USER_COPY` mode kept an elevated reference count, allowing stale operations and triggering warnings.

Here is the patch:
 
 static bool ublk_check_and_reset_active_ref(struct ublk_device *ub)
 {
 	int i, j;
 
-	if (!(ub->dev_info.flags & (UBLK_F_SUPPORT_ZERO_COPY |
-					UBLK_F_AUTO_BUF_REG)))
+	if (!ublk_dev_need_req_ref(ub))
 		return false;
 
 	for (i = 0; i < ub->dev_info.nr_hw_queues; i++) {
 		struct ublk_queue *ubq = ublk_get_queue(ub, i);
 
 		for (j = 0; j < ubq->q_depth; j++) {
 			struct ublk_io *io = &ubq->ios[j];
 			unsigned int refs = refcount_read(&io->ref) +
 				io->task_registered_buffers;
 
 			/*
 			 * UBLK_REFCOUNT_INIT or zero means no active
 			 * reference
 			 */
 			if (refs != UBLK_REFCOUNT_INIT && refs != 0)
 				return true;
 
 			/* reset to zero if the io hasn't active references */
 			refcount_set(&io->ref, 0);
 			io->task_registered_buffers = 0;
 		}
 	}
 	return false;
 }
